attempts.summary: Deployed a MariaDB Galera cluster on node1-node3 (bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster), created an appdb.orders table with an appuser account (password generated on-node via /dev/urandom), and verified multi-master writes replicate across all three. Added node4 by updating its galera.cnf (wsrep_cluster_address including all four hosts) and starting mariadb, which triggered an automatic SST (rsync) that fully copied the existing data; confirmed node4 can accept writes that replicate back to the original members. Opened firewalld ports 3306/4444/4567(tcp+udp)/4568 on all nodes (SELinux mysqld_port_t already covered them). Then ran the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on each of the 4 nodes one at a time: captured /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id and Galera health baseline, issued a delayed `systemctl reboot` so the ack returned first, polled until exec was available again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and verified the node rejoined the cluster (wsrep_cluster_size=4, state Synced, status Primary) with all appdb.orders rows intact before moving to the next node.
